note: For the '.zgnuhash' SHT_GNU_HASH section of the big-endian ELF64 input, elf_getdata triggers byte-order conversion of the 106-byte section data (EI_DATA=MSB on a little-endian host), producing the converted buffer that later code treats as initialized.
convert_data mallocs a size=106 destination buffer (uninitialized) and dispatches to elf_cvt_gnuhash with the raw section bytes as src; the whole buffer is later assumed converted.
First statement consuming attacker-controlled bytes: the 106-byte GNU hash section data (with attacker-controlled length) is read and byte-swapped into the destination.
Header word 2 (attacker-controlled, 0x0B000000 after conversion) selects how many 64-bit bloom words to convert; 11 words are converted before the length runs out.

The conversion stops with len=2 bytes still unconverted: the early return leaves the last 2 bytes of the destination buffer never written. The violated safety obligation is that the whole input (all len bytes) must be copied so the destination is fully initialized (len should reach 0).

Later code treats the whole converted buffer as initialized compressed file data: buf_in = data->d_buf + 12 covers the uninitialized tail, and zlib inflate reads those bytes (MSan use-of-uninitialized-value at the stored-block length check).
